author: jtraglia
content: Yeah the bid & self-slashing are both in B. The proposer still has to equivocate though. If B were the only block, the builder would reveal for B and its payload would be included, so nothing is lost. The trick is to also sign A with the same bid and try to only show it to the builder, who reveals for A, but the rest of the network accepts B. If the builder waits for N% of the network to attest before revealing, this doesn't really work. It's a bit of a foot gun though and I think we should fix it.

author: jtraglia
content:
* At its slot, the proposer gets a signed bid from a builder.
* It signs two blocks, A and B, both carrying that same bid.
* In B, it also includes an attester slashing of itself, built from two conflicting attestations it signs.
* It sends A only to the builder, and B to everyone else.
* The builder sees A as the head and reveals its payload for A.
* The attesters vote for B, so B becomes canonical but has no payload.
* B still records the builder's payment, which is paid once B has enough votes.
* The A/B proof can't cancel the payment, because the proposer is already slashed on B's chain.
* The builder pays the proposer's fee recipient for a block without its payload.
